text:
Maya S: quick note from today's porting work: Go SDK streaming has two DX pain points we should address: ctx cancellation not unblocking Recv(), and awkward generator option builder ergonomics.
Owen P: can you share a minimal repro?
Maya S: yes. here's the gist from our sample app:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
stream, err := client.Generator("realtime").Stream(ctx, prompt)
if err != nil { return err }
go func() {
  for {
    t, err := stream.Recv()
    if err != nil { log.Printf("recv err: %v", err); return }
    emit(t.Text)
  }
}()
// later
cancel() // goroutine doesn't exit quickly, hangs on network read
```
Maya S: after repeated open/close we saw goroutine growth and OOM risk.
Renee H: sounds like Read() isn't unblocked on ctx.Done(). We added a cancelable reader in JS; Go didn't get the same fix yet. Also the transport retry middleware retries streaming requests which can cause duplicated partial events when auth refreshes.
Owen P: proposed fixes: 1) transport-level cancelable io.Reader that returns ctx.Err() when canceled, 2) disable automatic retries for streaming requests (opt-in for apps that want it), 3) improve ergonomics: StreamController with Start/Close and RecvWith(ctx, timeout) so callers can control per-read deadlines.
Maya S: RecvWith would be great for backpressure and onboarding docs. current examples only show the naive loop and confuse newcomers.
Renee H: agree. let's also add a tiny example in examples/go/streaming/cancel-demo that demonstrates proper patterns and add a test asserting no goroutine leak after cancel.
Owen P: I'll open an issue and a PR for the cancelable reader + WithNoRetry option and add the example. ETA 48 hours.
Maya S: thanks. created issue #501 with logs and a small harness. @Owen P @Renee H
ci-bot: issue created (#501) and assigned to Owen P; label "devex" added.
Maya S: will follow up with the sample PR and a short quickstart note: "Prefer RecvWith or call Close() to avoid goroutine leaks."
Renee H: also add CHANGELOG note and align docs with JS/Python so parity is clear.
Owen P: noted. I'll proto and tag you both.
